title: Complete summary – Ultrasound, CT, MRI & nuclear medicine
html:
Built by reverse-engineering every MCQ of this lecture (the biggest chapter: 69 questions). 🔁 = asked in several sessions · ⚠ = classic trap.

Source of information & vocabulary 🔁🔁

TechniqueSource of informationVocabulary
Radiography / CTX-rays (X-ray tube)opacity / density (CT, HU)
Ultrasoundultrasound waves (piezoelectric transducer)echogenicity; anechoic, transsonic (= liquid)
MRIradiofrequency (radio) waves emitted by relaxing protons – NOT the magnetic field, NOT "resonance" ⚠signal: hypo-, hyper-, iso-signal / intensity (never "density")
Nuclear medicinegamma rays from a radiopharmaceutical inside the patientuptake / activity
  • "Transsonic" = liquid; it does NOT describe a solid, elastic, rigid or moving structure.

Ultrasound 🔁🔁

  • High-frequency sound, piezoelectric transducer; higher frequency = better resolution, less depth. Air blocks the beam; bone stops it (shadow). Non-ionising.
  • Vocabulary: anechoic = no echoes (fluid); hyperechoic; posterior acoustic shadow behind stones; posterior enhancement behind cysts. "Isodense" is NOT a US word.
  • Simple cyst: anechoic, thin wall, posterior enhancement, no flow.
  • Limits: obesity, uncooperative patient, air/bowel gas, operator dependence. NOT limits: surgical scars, sweaty skin, radiation (none) ⚠
  • Leading applications: gallbladder pathology, bile duct dilatation, follow-up of cirrhosis, HCC screening, hydronephrosis. NOT: staging of pancreatic tumours (= CT/MRI) ⚠
  • Doppler: information = FREQUENCY shift of the echoes (not phase, amplitude, colour) → blood flow velocity & direction; colour Doppler codes direction; power Doppler more sensitive to slow flow; no contrast needed.
  • Vessel lumen without contrast: MRI and (power) Doppler US. CT, DSA, radiography need contrast.

CT 🔁

  • Source: X-rays; density in Hounsfield units (not Kerma units).
  • HU: water 0, air −1000, fat ≈ −100 (darker than water – never 0 or +100), bone +400 to +1000.
  • Windows (post-processing, do NOT change dose): lung window also detects air outside the lung (pneumothorax, pneumoperitoneum), soft-tissue window, bone window.
  • Oral contrast: standard barium (or water-soluble iodine).
  • Phases: arterial 25–35 s, portal venous 60–70 s, excretory 5–10 min.
  • Artefacts: beam hardening (cupping, dark streaks – a CT artefact only), motion, metal streaks, partial volume. Chemical shift = MRI.
  • Advantages: fast, emergency, lung & bone cortex, multiplanar reconstructions. Ionising; soft-tissue contrast inferior to MRI.

MRI 🔁🔁

  • Strong magnetic field; protons excited by a radiofrequency pulse; signal from relaxing protons; gradients localise the signal. No X-rays.
  • Bright on T1: fat (hyperintense), subacute haemorrhage (methaemoglobin), melanin, gadolinium-enhanced tissue.
  • Dark on T1: simple fluid, tendons, calcifications, cortical bone, air.
  • T2: fluid & oedema bright; cortical bone & air dark; fat relatively bright unless fat-sat.
  • Cortical bone: hyposignal on T1 AND T2.
  • MRI superior to radiography/CT for: articular cartilage, bone oedema, early sacroiliitis. CT/radiography better for cortex and fractures.
  • MRCP: heavily T2-weighted, static fluid bright, no contrast, non-invasive.
  • Biliary cyst appears black on: T1 MRI and ultrasound (anechoic); bright on T2; dark grey on CT; invisible on X-ray.
  • Contraindications: non-MR-conditional pacemaker, ferromagnetic aneurysm clip, metal in the eye, most cochlear implants. Titanium prostheses OK; many pacemakers are now MR-conditional (not all unsafe).
  • Pregnancy: no ionising radiation (not a contraindication for that reason); RF burns possible with bad positioning; used with gadolinium; slower than CT.

Nuclear medicine 🔁🔁🔁

  • Radiopharmaceutical = pharmaceutical bound to a radioisotope, used in nuclear medicine; NOT a contrast agent, NOT for US.
  • Source of radiation = inside the patient; image = detection by the gamma camera of gamma rays coming from the patient. Diagnostic (not irradiating tumours). Functional information.
  • Tc-99m: T½ 6 h, 140 keV, pure gamma emitter.
  • SPECT/CT = hybrid technique, nuclear-medicine diagnostic procedure (not contrast CT, not whole-body scan, not therapy). Other hybrids: PET/CT, PET/MRI.
  • FDG PET-CT: hybrid morphofunctional; metabolic activity of viable tumour cells; uptake ∝ aggressiveness; main role in oncology (staging, response, digestive cancers).
  • Parathyroid adenoma: gold standard = Tc-99m MIBI (sestamibi) scintigraphy.

Bone scintigraphy

  • Agent Tc-99m MDP/HMDP (not pertechnetate); images 2–4 h after injection; static, whole skeleton in one exam.
  • Main indication: bone metastases (prostate, breast); also osteosarcoma, infection, fractures; benign and malignant. Very sensitive, early (before X-ray). Gives metabolic information.
  • A normal scan shows skeleton + kidneys + bladder + soft tissues ("all of the above").
  • Contraindicated in pregnancy; renal failure is not the main contraindication; feasible in children; NOT the first-step exam for primary bone tumours (= radiograph) ⚠

Renal scintigraphy 🔁

  • Dynamic (Tc-99m DTPA / MAG3): differential (split) renal function + diagnosis of obstruction (diuretic renography); irradiates ~10× less than urography. NOT for stones/tumours (stones = CT), absolute function not the main purpose.
  • Static (Tc-99m DMSA, images at 2–3 h): renal cortical scars after urinary tract infection.

Lung V/Q scintigraphy

  • Perfusion agent: Tc-99m MAA (macroaggregated albumin, NOT "CTPA"), injected slowly i.v., lodges in pre-capillary arterioles (~0.1 %), cleared by hydrolysis and phagocytosis.
  • Normal V/Q essentially excludes recent significant PE; emboli multiple (90 %), bilateral (85 %), more in lower lobes. It does NOT detect lung metastases.

Interventional radiology

  • Guidance: US, CT, fluoroscopy, MRI – never "blinded".
  • First step of any vascular intervention: Doppler US.
  • Ideal biopsy needle: the safest (smallest diameter) giving the necessary (not maximal) diagnostic information.
  • Before any procedure: clinical history, objectives, imaging of the lesion, technical feasibility – NOT "achieve the goal no matter what".
